subject: Clarify: per-tenant short-term log snapshot for compliance review
messages:
From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@cyberialabs.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@cyberialabs.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: short-term per-tenant log snapshot for upcoming audit

Hi Irene,

We have an external compliance review scheduled with our auditor the week of 2026-09-20. They asked for a time-bounded snapshot of tenant-scoped inference logs (request/response metadata and routing traces) for a 30-day window (2026-08-15 to 2026-09-14) to validate retention & deletion practices.

Two quick constraints from our side:
- The snapshot needs to be tenant-scoped (only our tenant data).
- PII should either be redacted or clearly documented in a manifest so we can evaluate redaction feasibility.

Can Redwood produce a signed, tamper-evident manifest and a secure transfer (SFTP or signed HTTPS bundle) for this window? Also please advise on how you demonstrate deletion of earlier data (audit hashes, manifest of deleted objects, or certificate).

Thanks — appreciate a quick confirmation and any lead time required.

Sam Patel
Head of Security Operations
Cyberia Labs
sam.patel@cyberialabs.com

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@cyberialabs.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term per-tenant log snapshot for upcoming audit

Sam — thanks for the clear ask. We can support a tenant-scoped snapshot with the properties you listed; below is a proposed scope and deliverables so you can confirm: 

Proposed deliverables:
- Tenant-only archive (gzip) containing: request metadata, routing traces, model-variant IDs, and system-level error codes for the 2026-08-15 to 2026-09-14 window. We will not include full request prompt text by default unless you request it explicitly.
- A manifest.csv with SHA256 hashes for each object and a per-file encryption header (KMS key id).
- A signed attestment PDF (PKCS7) stating our snapshot generation time and the queries used to isolate tenant data.
- Optional redaction: we can run a PII redaction pass (removal/replace) if you provide the fields you consider PII — note this adds 2 business days.
- Delivery methods: secure SFTP push to a customer-managed host, or a time-limited signed HTTPS bundle (expires after 7 days).
- Proof of prior deletions: we can provide manifests and historical deletion markers for the tenant for the previous retention windows (up to 12 months), plus a short description of our retention enforcement (automated TTL job + immutable deletion markers).

Lead time & considerations:
- Standard snapshot generation (no redaction): 3 business days.
- With PII redaction and manifest verification: 5 business days.
- Encrypted archive uses your KMS key if you can provide a key-wrap (otherwise we encrypt to our KMS and include key metadata).
- If the auditor needs attestations tied to SOC 2 controls or CAIQ mappings, let us know which control IDs are required and we will include crosswalks in the attestation.

I am attaching the snapshot-schema.csv to show the file/field layout we propose (attached). Jonas/V can you confirm the generation cadence and whether we need Legal on the signed attestation?

— Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Security Partnerships
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwood.ai

Attachments: snapshot-schema.csv (schema preview)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: Cyberia snapshot — generation plan and legal check

Jonas / Vanessa — looping you in to confirm operational feasibility and legal requirements. Key points: 

Operational notes:
- We can run a tenant-scoped export from the cold log store and streaming KV cache. The export will produce ~12GB compressed for a 30-day window at Cyberia's current volume.
- We will include per-object SHA256 and our signing key. If Cyberia wants to provide their KMS key, we should do key-wrap at creation; otherwise we will encrypt with Redwood KMS and provide key metadata.
- Redaction is doable but non-trivial — it requires field-level rules. I estimate +2 days and a small infra cost.

Legal/compliance ask:
- Do we need a formal attestation signed by Legal? Cyberia mentioned SOC 2 mapping in their initial note. If the auditor wants a CAIQ/SIG crosswalk bundled with the snapshot attestation, Legal should draft the language — tagging Legal if needed.

Action items:
1) Jonas: confirm the export job window and whether we can produce the signed manifest (SHA + PKCS7) by 2026-09-17.
2) Vanessa: confirm whether Customer Success needs to approve the data scope and whether we should present redaction options to Cyberia.
3) I will draft the attestation template (non-legal wording) and the SFTP instructions. I attached the internal evidence_playbook.pdf excerpt showing prior snapshots for reference.

Irene

Attachments: evidence_playbook.pdf (internal playbook excerpt)

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@cyberialabs.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: security@cyberialabs.com
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 17:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term per-tenant log snapshot for upcoming audit

Irene — this looks good, thank you. We will accept:
- Tenant-only gzip archive (no raw prompts unless requested)
- Manifest.csv with SHA256 hashes and KMS metadata
- PKCS7-signed attestation PDF referencing SOC 2 control mapping (we'll send the specific control IDs tomorrow)
- Delivery via SFTP (we will provide credentials)

Please proceed with the standard snapshot cadence (3 business days). We prefer encryption with our KMS key; I'll coordinate with our cloud team on key wrap. Also please include the manifest of deletions for preceding rolling windows (the auditor asked for samples from prior quarters).

If you can, include brief notes in the attestation about how TTL enforcement works (what jobs/processes cause deletions and how deletion manifests are generated).

Sam
Head of Security Operations
Cyberia Labs
